claims.text: Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation will reduce the coefficient of friction of a high-entropy alloy.
Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation will reduce the wear rate of a high-entropy alloy.
Forming an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer will reduce the coefficient of friction of a high-entropy alloy.
Forming an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer will reduce the wear rate of a high-entropy alloy.
The proposed tribological improvement will remain effective from -20°C to 200°C.
The intervention produces a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation or an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The nanohierarchical architecture enhances the alloy's self-lubricating properties.
The ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer enhances the alloy's self-lubricating properties.
The proposed surface structures reduce the contact area between the alloy surface and the counterface.
Reducing the alloy-counterface contact area decreases the coefficient of friction.
Reducing the alloy-counterface contact area decreases the wear rate.
The treated alloy will have a 30% lower coefficient of friction than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will have a 40% lower wear rate than the untreated alloy.
The untreated high-entropy alloy is the comparison baseline.

contradictions.description: The intervention and mediator describe nanohierarchical architecture and an ultra-nanocrystalline layer as alternatives using 'or,' whereas the mechanism refers to both structures together using 'and,' leaving unclear whether either treatment alone or their combination is required.
